summary: A write-up of a Wellness Workshop on sleep hygiene held September 15, 2023 at a local community center, led by sleep therapist Dr. Sonia Ray. She presented ten surprising bedroom factors that sabotage sleep, from blue light and clutter to caffeine, alcohol, light intrusion and allergens. Attendees left motivated to make changes like decluttering, replacing pillows and setting meal and caffeine curfews.
one_line: Dr. Sonia Ray's September 2023 community workshop revealed ten hidden bedroom habits and conditions that disrupt sleep and how to fix them.
key_facts: The sleep hygiene Wellness Workshop was held on September 15, 2023 at a local community center.
Dr. Sonia Ray, described as a renowned sleep therapist, directed the workshop.
The workshop covered ten surprising bedroom culprits that may sabotage sleep.
Blue light from electronic devices hinders production of melatonin, the hormone crucial for sleep.
Clutter such as laundry, books and knick-knacks can turn a bedroom into a stress-inducing jungle; a tidy room equals a tranquil mind.
Attendee John Archer realized his neck pain came from his ancient pillow, not from age.
Sleep expert Emma Lopez illustrated that an uncomfortable or worn-out mattress can ruin a night's rest; people spend about a third of their lives in bed.
Dr. Ray recommended the 'Goldilocks Zone' of bedroom temperature, avoiding extremes of hot or cold.
Heavy, spicy or sugary foods close to bedtime can disrupt sleep, while snacks of complex carbs, dairy or nuts may promote it.
Attendee Michael Thompson learned his 'sleepy-time' tea contained caffeine, contributing to his late-night wakefulness; caffeine also hides in teas, sodas and certain medications.
Alcohol may help you doze off but hampers the depth and quality of the sleep cycle, leading to less restorative sleep.
Light from streetlamps or digital clocks can trick internal clocks; blackout curtains became popular, as did interest in hypoallergenic bedding to combat dust mites and mold.
